title: Staggered GPU Takeout Plan - Regional Cooldowns Q1 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working doc outlines a staggered "takeout" approach for planned GPU maintenance windows across regions, focusing on minimizing customer impact while allowing driver upgrades, kernel rollforward, and thermal/cooling validation. Unlike previous bulk-drain schedules, we propose smaller, overlapping waves with hot-spare routing and cross-region burst capacity.

High-level goals:
- Keep regional latency SLOs met (p95 < 120ms for hosted-api critical routes)
- Limit sustained regional capacity loss to <= 18% per active wave
- Provide safe rollback for driver upgrades within 45 minutes per wave
- Validate cooling behavior after driver/firmware changes with 24h soak on small cohort

Wave model (recommended):
- Wave size: 8–12 racks (or equivalent 10–18% of regional GPU inventory)
- Wave duration: 6 hours maintenance window + 2 hour post-soak observations
- Overlap: Start waves in adjacent regions staggered by >= 2 hours to enable cross-region burst without simultaneous global drop
- Max concurrent waves: 3 (no two waves in same geo-subnet)

Example regional schedule (week-of rollout):
- Monday 00:00 - 08:00 UTC: APAC-east (wave A)
- Monday 02:00 - 10:00 UTC: EU-west (wave B)
- Monday 04:00 - 12:00 UTC: US-central (wave C)
Note: windows chosen to align with local off-peak and to allow routing fallback to adjacent zones.

Capacity mitigation strategies:
1) Warm spare pool: Maintain a 10% reserved pool of Dedicated capacity that can be routed in-hosted for emergency bursts.
2) Cross-region burst policy: Auto-shift non-low-latency batch workloads to next-nearest region when regional free capacity < 15%.
3) Pre-warm fallback flavors: Keep a small pool of quantized model variants hot in partner regions for fast failover.
4) Progressive traffic shift: For canary driver builds, shift 20% traffic off affected racks before kernel roll to catch regressions.

Driver upgrade flow (per wave):
- Pre-checks (T-72h): inventory, recent error trends, thermal logs, existing kernel patch level; create rollback image.
- T-4h: mark racks for drain, notify on-call, create Jira shard INF-4621-waveX.
- T-1h: begin graceful connection draining for active sessions; pause autoscale down for unaffected pools.
- +0m: power-cycle drivers with staged firmware; run smoke-runner tests against sample prompts.
- +30m: if smoke passes, move 30% of production traffic back; if failure, rollback to previous driver immediately and escalate.
- +6h: full post-maintenance soak + health probes; collect perf telemetry for 24h.

Rollback and emergency abort criteria:
- Increase in 5xx error rate > 0.8 percentage points relative to baseline for > 10 minutes.
- Median p99 token latency regression > 45% sustained > 5 minutes.
- Thermal threshold breach on > 3% of affected GPUs.
If any trigger fires: abort wave, re-image to previous driver, and re-route traffic. Target time-to-rollback: <= 45 minutes.

Validation & telemetry to collect:
- Pre/post token-level latency distributions (p50/p95/p99) per route
- GPU utilization and power draw, per-card
- KV cache hit/miss delta (some regressions surface as cache thrash)
- Error taxonomy (OOM, CUDA errors, driver timeouts)
- 1-hour, 6-hour, 24-hour soak snapshots to confirm stability

Communication plan:
- Pre-run: 48h email + slack #infra-notify (wave details, affected regions, expected capacity loss)
- During: live-update thread in #infra-ops, and brief status every 60 minutes
- Post: incident summary doc with telemetry, root cause (if any), and follow-ups within 48h

Risk matrix (top items):
- Risk: Cross-region burst fails due to peering limits — Mitigation: verify bandwidth reservations 24h prior, pre-coordinate with cloud-net.
- Risk: Driver regression causing increased token cost — Mitigation: run synthetic cost-eval harness during canary stage.
- Risk: Customers on Dedicated seeing degraded tail latency — Mitigation: honor dedicated SLA by shifting queries to spare dedicated pool and credit customers per SLA terms.

Open decisions / TODOs (working list):
- Finalize warm-spare funding for Dedicated pool (finance approval needed) — owner: Priya Singh
- Confirm peering bandwidth reservations with cloud partners for Jan–Mar 2026 maintenance — owner: Ethan Brooks
- Add automated rollback runbook to gitops repo and test in staging cluster — owner: Sofia Martinez

Appendix: quick capacity table (region / total GPUs / planned wave takeout / post-wave available)
| region     | total gpus | planned takeout | expected available |
|------------|------------|-----------------|--------------------|
| APAC-east  | 4,200      | 560 (13%)       | 3,640              |
| EU-west    | 6,800      | 950 (14%)       | 5,850              |
| US-central | 9,600      | 1,440 (15%)     | 8,160              |

Notes: numbers above are draft estimates — confirm exact rack-to-GPU mapping before final scheduling.

End of doc — please leave inline comments for schedule conflicts or capacity adjustments.
